title: Mother's Day Raspberry Rose Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes with a raspberry cream swirl and rosewater frosting, ready in about 45 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes are my go to for Mother's Day brunch tables. A soft vanilla cake gets a swirl of raspberry cream baked right into the middle, so every bite has a fruity surprise.
ingredients: 2 tbsp heavy cream, for jam swirl
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add flour mix and milk in alternating batches. Mix just until smooth.
Stir the raspberry jam with 2 tablespoons heavy cream until pourable.
Fill liners two thirds full with batter. Drop a small spoonful of raspberry mix on top of each and swirl gently with a toothpick.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat butter for frosting until pale, about 2 minutes. Add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in heavy cream and rosewater. Beat 2 more minutes until fluffy. Add a touch of pink coloring if you like.
Pipe frosting on fully cooled cupcakes. Top each with a fresh raspberry.
tips: Use a light hand with rosewater. Too much tastes like perfume, not dessert.
Swirl the jam gently. Overmixing turns the top muddy instead of marbled.
Chill the frosting 10 minutes before piping if your kitchen is warm, for cleaner swirls.
Swap fresh raspberries for freeze dried ones on top if fresh fruit is out of season.

faq.question: Can I use rose extract instead of rosewater?
faq.answer: Yes, but use half the amount. Rose extract is stronger than rosewater, so start with 1/4 teaspoon and taste the frosting before adding more.

faq.question: Why did my raspberry swirl sink to the bottom?
faq.answer: The jam mix was likely too thin. Keep the cream added to a minimum so the swirl stays thick enough to sit near the top of the batter.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead for Mother's Day brunch?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store covered at room temperature. Frost the morning you serve them for the best texture.

faq.question: What can I use instead of fresh raspberries for garnish?
faq.answer: Freeze dried raspberries, a small edible flower, or a light drizzle of extra jam all work well if fresh berries are not available.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring a soft floral touch to any Mother's Day table. The raspberry swirl keeps them from tasting too sweet, and the rosewater frosting makes them feel special without much extra work.
